objective: Proof and computation. A ring (a prism minus a line) spliced onto a grid through one 3-edge cut: by the reduction lemma the grid acts as the missing line, so from the ring's cut point the halo of an opened handle is the full ladder halo, running along the whole far face of the ring for every ring length. Check for rings of 16 to 64 points.
status: Proved by STRIP-RELAY-20261103-001B-P001: a ring (a prism minus a line) spliced onto a grid sees itself as the closed prism, since the grid acts as the removed line (reduction lemma); so from the middle point of the removed line the far halo of an opened Fano handle is the far part of the long face holding that line's far corner, k - 3 lines along the whole ring (ladder law). Checked on rings over 16- to 64-cycles: exactly one point creates off the faces around it in the spliced space, that cut point, at k - 3 ring lines
title: Pendant rings
